Rashi on Shabbat 138b:10:1.english: In the vineyard - Because they used to sit [in] rows [upon] rows, like a vineyard.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:11:1.hebrew: זו הלכה - כדכתיב (דברים ה׳:ה׳) [להגיד לכם] את דבר ה', דהיינו תורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:11:1.english: That is halakha - As it is written (Deuteronomy 5:5): "[to tell you] the word of the Lord," which is Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:11:2.english: That is prophecy - As it is written (Hosea 1[:1]): "The word of the Lord that came to Hosea," etc.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:11:3.english: That is the end [of days] - I do not know from where [it is derived].

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:13:1.hebrew: בהדיא כתיב - ותורה שבכתב הרי כתובה ומונחת, יקראו ויראו:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:13:1.english: It is explicitly written - And the Written Torah is indeed written and set down [before them]; let them read [it] and see.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:14:1.hebrew: שהתנור תחלה - שנטמא מן האויר, כדכתיב (ויקרא יא) "אל תוכו", והוא חוזר ומטמא אוכלין שבתוכו מן האויר:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:14:1.english: For the oven [is] first-degree [impure] - For it became impure through [its] airspace, as it is written (Leviticus 11): "into its midst"; and it in turn renders food inside it impure through [its] airspace.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:15:1.hebrew: כמאן דמלי טומאה - כשנפל השרץ באוירו, דהא בלא נגיעה מטמא, והלכך כמאן דמלי טומאה הוא ותהוי פת ראשונה:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:15:1.english: As one filled with impurity - When the creeping animal fell into its airspace, for it transmits impurity without contact, and therefore it is as though it is filled with impurity and the bread becomes first-[degree impure].

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:1.hebrew: לא ס"ד - למיהוי כמאן דמלי טומאה:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:1.english: It does not enter your mind - [for the oven] to be [considered] as though filled with ritual impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:2.hebrew: דתניא יכול יהו כל הכלים טמאים מאויר כלי חרס - שאם היה כלי אחר בתוכו, שיטמא מחמת השרץ שבאויר החיצון, או מחמת שיטמאנו אויר כלי החיצון שהוא טמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:2.english: As it was taught [in a baraita]: One might [think] that all vessels become ritually impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel - That if another vessel was inside it, it would become ritually impure on account of the creeping animal that is in the airspace of the outer [vessel], or on account of the airspace of the outer vessel—which is [itself] ritually impure—rendering it ritually impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:3.hebrew: תלמוד לומר כל אשר בתוכו יטמא - וסמיך ליה "מכל האוכל אשר יאכל" — אוכלין ומשקין שבתוכו טמאים ולא כלים. שמע מינה תרתי: חדא, דלא אמרינן חזייה כמאן דמלי טומאה, דאם כן, אם כלי שטף הוא הפנימי שמטמא מגבו, יהא טמא, דהא נגע בטומאה. אלא לא אמרינן חזייה כמאן דמלי טומאה, ואוכלין ומשקין שבחיצון הוא דמטמאי מחמת הכלי, שהכלי ראשון והם שניים, אבל כלים לא; דהואיל דאין טומאה זו באה אלא מחמת הכלי, אשמעינן האי קרא שאין כלי שאינו אב הטומאה מטמא כלי:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:16:3.english: The verse states: "All that is in it shall be impure" - And juxtaposed to it is [the verse]: "All food that is eaten" — foods and liquids that are inside it become impure, but not vessels. We learn two things from this: First, that we do not say "view it as though it were full of impurity"; for if so, if the inner [vessel] is a rinsable vessel, which can contract impurity from its outside, it would become impure, since it is touching the impurity. Rather, we do not say "view it as though it were full of impurity," and it is [only] foods and liquids in the outer [vessel] that become impure on account of the vessel — for the vessel is a first-degree [impurity] and they are second-degree — whereas vessels do not [become impure]; for since this impurity comes only on account of the vessel, this verse teaches us that a vessel which is not a primary source of impurity does not render another vessel impure.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:1:1.hebrew: כילת חתנים - לא דמיא לשאר כילות, ששאר כילות פרוסות על גבי קינוף שהיא לד' רגלים ויש לה גג, דהוי אהל. ושל חתנים על גבי נקליטין, שאינם אלא שנים באמצעית המטה, וקנה נתון עליהם, והבגד נתון עליו ונופל לכאן ולכאן, ואין לה גג טפח. הלכך, לאו אהל הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:1:1.english: A bridegroom's canopy - It is not similar to other canopies, for other canopies are spread over a frame [kinuf] that has four legs, and it has a roof, which is [considered] a tent. Whereas [a canopy] of bridegrooms [is spread] over naklitin, which are only two [poles] in the middle of the bed, with a rod placed upon them, and the cloth is placed over it and drapes down to this side and that, so it does not have a roof [the width of] a handbreadth. Therefore, it is not a tent.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:1.hebrew: בפחות מג' - שהיא הולכת ומתפשטת למטה:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:1.english: Within less than three [handbreadths] - For it progressively widens downward.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:2.hebrew: ולא אמרן אלא שאין בשיפועה טפח - שאין כל צד וצד נפשט למטה להתרחק טפח מכנגד אמצעיתו, דהיינו שאין ברחבו למטה טפחיים. וכילת חתנים אינה עשויה לישן תחתיה:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:2.english: And we only said [this] where there is not a handbreadth in its incline - That each side does not spread downward to distance [itself] a handbreadth from opposite its center, that is, its width at the bottom is not two handbreadths. And a bridal canopy is not made to sleep under it.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:3.hebrew: אבל נחתא מפוריא טפח - ההוא טפח הוה קיר לאהל, והמטה נעשית לו גג:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:2:3.english: However, [if] it descends a handbreadth from the bed - That handbreadth is a wall for a tent, and the bed becomes a roof for it.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:3:1.english: Siyana - A felt hat, feltres [in Old French].

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:3:2.hebrew: אסור - לצאת בו בשבת, ולקמיה מפרש ואזיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:3:2.english: Prohibited - To go out with it on Shabbat, and further on [the Gemara] proceeds to explain [it].

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:3:3.hebrew: הא דאית ביה טפח - שהוא מתפשט להלן מראשו טפח, אסור משום אהלא:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:3:3.english: This [case] where it has a handbreadth - [meaning] that it extends beyond his head [by] a handbreadth, [it is] prohibited on account of [forming] a tent.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:4:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה שרביב בגלימיה טפח - הניח טליתו על ראשו כדרך שהוא מתעטף, והרחיקה להלן מראשו טפח:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:4:1.english: But if so, [if] one extended his cloak a handbreadth - [That is, he] placed his tallit on his head in the manner that he wraps himself [in it], and extended it further from his head [by] a handbreadth.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:4:2.hebrew: אלא - טעמא לאו משום אהל הוא, אלא משום שלא יגביהנו הרוח מראשו ואתי לאתויי ארבע אמות. הלכך, מיהדק בראשו שפיר — שרי; לא מיהדק — אסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:4:2.english: Rather - the reason is not because of [making a] tent, rather [out of concern] lest the wind lift it from his head and he come to carry [it] four cubits. Therefore, [if] it is fastened firmly on his head, it is permitted; [if] it is not fastened [firmly], it is prohibited.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:5:1.hebrew: תרתי בשבת וחדא בתורה - שהיית רגיל לומר שני דברים משמו בהלכות שבת, ואחת בתורה, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:5:1.english: Two on Shabbat and one on the Torah - That you were accustomed to say two things in his name regarding the laws of Shabbat, and one regarding the Torah, as [follows] below.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:1.english: A wineskin by its straps - A wineskin with its straps, and [it is] placed on its fixed place.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:2.hebrew: מותר לנטותו בשבת - והא דאמרן לעיל פטור אבל אסור, היכא דלא הוי מתוקן בכיסנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:2.english: It is permitted to spread it on Shabbat - And that which we said earlier, [that it is] exempt but prohibited, [applies] where it is not prepared with straps.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:3.hebrew: בב' בני אדם - לא מימתח ליה שפיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:3.english: By two people - [It] is not stretched well.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:4.hebrew: באדם אחד - ממתח ליה שפיר, שמותחו על יתד זו וקושרו בה, וחוזר ומותחו על זו וקושרו בה. כך פירשו רבותי, וכן מצאתי בתשובת הגאונים, ואיני יודע מהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:6:4.english: By one person - He stretches it well, for he stretches it over this peg and ties it to it, and then stretches it over that [peg] and ties it to it. Thus my teachers explained, and so I found in a responsum of the Geonim, and I do not know what it is.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:8:1.english: The other - [that] of Shabbat, what is it?

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:8:2.english: Of its legs - Its supports, [which are] like legs.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:8:3.hebrew: שמא יתקע - כשמחבר לה הרגל, יתקענה בחוזק והוי בונה. אבל (ת"ק) היכא דלא נשמטה אלא אחת, לא חייש למתקע כולי האי:
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:8:3.english: Lest one fasten - When he attaches the leg to it, he will fasten it firmly, and it constitutes building. However, [according to] (the Tanna Kamma), where only one [leg] fell out, he is not concerned about fastening [it] so firmly.

Rashi on Shabbat 138b:9:1.hebrew: הפלא ופלא - סיפא דקרא, "ואבדה חכמת חכמיו":
Rashi on Shabbat 138b:9:1.english: Wondrous astonishment - The end of the verse [states]: "and the wisdom of its wise shall be lost."

Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:11:1.hebrew: דבר ה' זה הקץ - דכתיב גבי גלות שבעים: "לכלות דבר ה' מפי ירמיה" (עזרא א׳:א׳). מ"ר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:11:1.english: "The word of the Lord" — that is the end - For it is written regarding the seventy[-year] exile: "to fulfill the word of the Lord spoken by Jeremiah" (Ezra 1:1). [From] my teacher.

Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:2:1.hebrew: שאין בשיפועה טפח - הרבה יש תימה: איך יתכן זה? דא"כ, למה הוא ראוי אם לכל השיפוע אין טפח? ויש לפרש: כגון שהסדין שפרוס על הכילה מונח על גבי קנים מרובים, ולא פשטו הסדין היטב, ומונח ונופל בין קנה לקנה כעין שורות, דיש עכשיו בין כל קנה שיפוע, ואין באותו שיפוע טפח; ודוחק. וי"מ שאין בשיפוע טפח בגובה י', דכשיצא השיפוע טפח אין משם עד למטה גובה י', דלא חשיב אהל, כדאשכחן בפ"ק דסוכה (דף י.), דבכילה כי הך מותר לישן בסוכה, דאמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: "מותר לישן בכילת חתנים אע"פ שיש לה גג, והוא שאינה י' טפחים". ואין נראה לר"י, דודאי נהי דגבי סוכה לא חשיב אהל, וכן לגבי ק"ש כדאיתא התם (דף.:), מיהו לגבי שבת חשיב ואסירי, שהרי משמרת וביעתא וקידרא וחביתא אסירי משום אהל, ולא משמע שיש בגובהן י' טפחים. מ"ר. ועוד קשה מדלקמן גבי כפיפה מצרית. ובשם רבינו שמואל פי' דל"ג להאי לישנא כלל "שיפועי אהלים כאהלים דמו", דבסוף פ"ק דסוכה (דף יט:) מסקינן דשיפוע אהלים לאו כאהלים דמו. ואי משום הא לא איריא, דיש לפרש דהתם באין בשיפועו טפח, והכא כשיש בשיפועו טפח:
Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:2:1.english: Where there is not in its incline a handbreadth - There is great wonder: how is this possible? For if so, what is it fit for if the entire incline does not have a handbreadth? One can explain [that it refers to a case] such as where the sheet spread over the canopy rests upon many reeds, and they did not stretch the sheet well, so it rests and sags between reed and reed like rows, such that there is now an incline between each reed, and in that incline there is not a handbreadth — and [this explanation is] forced. And some explain that there is not a handbreadth in the incline within a height of ten [handbreadths], for when the incline extends out a handbreadth, there is not from there downward a height of ten [handbreadths], so it is not considered a tent — as we find in the first chapter of Sukkah (10a), that in a canopy like this it is permitted to sleep in a sukkah, for Rav Yehudah said in the name of Shmuel: "It is permitted to sleep in a bridal canopy even though it has a roof, provided that it is not ten handbreadths [high]." But this does not appear [correct] to the Ri, for certainly, granted that regarding a sukkah it is not considered a tent — and likewise regarding the recitation of Shema, as is stated there (ibid.) — nevertheless, regarding Shabbat it is considered [a tent] and they are prohibited, for behold, a strainer, an egg, a pot, and a barrel are prohibited on account of [forming] a tent, and it is not implied that their height is ten handbreadths. [So I heard from] my teacher. And furthermore, it is difficult from [what is stated] below regarding an Egyptian basket. And in the name of Rabbeinu Shmuel, [he] explained that we do not read this wording at all: "the inclines of tents are considered like tents," for at the end of the first chapter of Sukkah (19b) we conclude that the incline of tents is not considered like tents. Yet if because of that [alone], it is not a proof, for one can explain that there [it is speaking] of where there is not a handbreadth in its incline, whereas here [it is speaking] of where there is a handbreadth in its incline:

Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:4:1.hebrew: הא דמהדק - פירש ר"ח: שאינו נכפף, דאז נראה כעין אהל; דלא מהדק — שהוא נכפף, ואז אין נראה כעין אהל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 138b:4:1.english: Where it is firm - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: [This means] that it does not bend, for then it appears like a kind of tent; [and where it is] not firm — [this means] that it bends, and then it does not appear like a kind of tent.
